title: Boats & the Harbour
strapline: Load the cargo, sail the harbour, dock at the quay — journeys across the water in a small-world sea.
intent: A small-world harbour lets children explore journeys across water, loading and unloading cargo, sailing between ports and telling stories on the sea.
Testing which boats float, sail and carry, and how much cargo they hold before they tip, folds real floating-and-sinking science into the play.
Loading, docking and manoeuvring boats in water builds hand-eye coordination and careful control.
Naming boats and their jobs — ferry, fishing boat, lifeboat, cargo ship — and the people who work them builds vocabulary and understanding of the world.
Positional and directional language flows naturally — across the harbour, under the bridge, alongside the quay, out to sea.
The harbour invites cooperative storytelling — voyages, rescues, deliveries — with each boat given a voice and a mission.
implementation: Set up a water tray or builder's tray as a harbour with a quay, jetties, a bridge and a mix of boats.
Add cargo to load — pebbles, crates, small-world people and animals — and let children test how much each boat carries before it tips.
Use precise names yourself — ferry, tug, trawler, lifeboat — and talk about who works on the water and how they help.
Narrate position and direction as you play alongside: 'she's sailing across to the far jetty, under the bridge, into the harbour'.
Stage a problem — a boat that won't float loaded, a rescue at sea — and let children solve it.
Add mark-making — flags, a harbour map, cargo lists — to give the play written jobs.
key_questions: How much cargo can this boat carry before it tips?
Which boats float best — and why do you think that is?
Can you sail her across the harbour, under the bridge and into the quay?
Who works on this boat, and what is their job?
There's a boat in trouble at sea — how could we rescue it?

impact.text: Children test which boats float and how much they carry before tipping — real floating-and-sinking science.
Children load, dock and manoeuvre boats in water, building hand-eye coordination and control.
Children name boats and their jobs and talk about the people who work on the water.
Children use positional and directional language — across, under, alongside, out to sea.
Children invent cooperative voyages, rescues and deliveries, giving each boat a voice and a mission.

enhancements: Cargo to load — pebbles, crates, small-world people — and a tipping-point challenge.
A harbour map, flags and cargo lists to give the play written jobs.
A staged problem — a boat that won't float loaded, a rescue at sea — for children to solve.
A bridge, jetties and a quay to sail between and manoeuvre around.
Boat books and pictures of real ferries, tugs, trawlers and lifeboats.

playing_exploring: Children sail, load and dock the boats freely, testing what floats and how much each will carry.
The harbour is an open sea of possibility — voyages, cargo and rescues to invent.
active_learning: Loading cargo without capsizing is an absorbing challenge, and children keep adjusting until the boat sails.
creating_thinking: Children narrate voyages and solve the harbour's problems — an overloaded boat, a rescue, a route round the bridge.
